## Maths, Statistics & Computer Science

- [Mike X Cohen] (https://www.youtube.com/@mikexcohen1)
  <details><summary>My thoughts</summary>Great for linear algebra, signal processing and data analysis with a neuroscience flavour. Very clear, very thorough.</details>
- [The Organic Chemistry Tutor] (https://www.youtube.com/@TheOrganicChemistryTutor)
  <details><summary>My thoughts</summary>My go-to when I need a topic explained step by step. Tons of worked examples, whatever the subject.</details>
- [3Blue1Brown](https://www.youtube.com/@3blue1brown)
  <details><summary>My thoughts</summary>Beautiful visual intuition for maths and neural networks. Watch it before the formal version.</details>
- [CS50: Introduction to Computer Science] (https://www.youtube.com/@cs50)
  <details><summary>My thoughts</summary>The best gentle introduction to CS I know. Lectures are engaging and the problem sets are great practice.</details>
- [Introduction to Statistical Learning](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=5N9V07EIfIg&list=PLOg0ngHtcqbPTlZzRHA2ocQZqB1D_qZ5V)
  <details><summary>My thoughts</summary>A friendly, practical intro to regression, classification and resampling. Pairs perfectly with the book.</details>
- [Theory of Computation](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=9syvZr-9xwk&list=PLUl4u3cNGP60_JNv2MmK3wkOt9syvfQWY)
  <details><summary>My thoughts</summary>Automata, grammars and Turing machines explained clearly. Also a nice bridge to formal linguistics.</details>

## Machine Learning & NLP

- [CS224N: Natural Language Processing with Deep Learning (Stanford)] (https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=DzpHeXVSC5I&list=PLoROMvodv4rOaMFbaqxPDoLWjDaRAdP9D)
  <details><summary>My thoughts</summary>The reference course for modern NLP, from word vectors to transformers. Demanding but worth it.</details>

## AI Safety

- [AI Evaluation Programme: Capabilities and Safety](https://www.youtube.com/@aievaluationorg)
  <details><summary>My thoughts</summary>Good for seeing how people actually test what AI models can do and where they fail. Very relevant to my interests.</details>

## Linguistics & Language Evolution

### Introductions

- [Introduction to Linguistics](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Mvy5hjAWeZw&list=PLUl4u3cNGP63BZGNOqrF2qf_yxOjuG35j)
  <details><summary>My thoughts</summary>A solid starting point covering phonetics through syntax and semantics. Good for building foundations.</details>
- [Language, Mind and Brain: the cognitive biology of language](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=z6rVdlSfmYo)
  <details><summary>My thoughts</summary>Looks at language as a biological capacity rather than just a system of rules. Made me think differently about what language even is.</details>

### Language evolution

- [How humans got language, Simon Kirby](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=ZIen7jJhvPM)
  <details><summary>My thoughts</summary>Shows how language structure can emerge through cultural transmission. Simple experiments, big ideas.</details>
- [Language evolution, big gods and rituals, Russell Gray](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=RGML2mMAaEI)
  <details><summary>My thoughts</summary>Uses phylogenetic methods borrowed from biology to study language and culture. A fun mix of disciplines.</details>

### Language learning & processing

- [A computational approach to early language bootstrapping](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=oclbYbGbxSE)
  <details><summary>My thoughts</summary>How models can explain the way babies get a foothold in language. Sits right where linguistics meets ML.</details>
- [Ecological language: a multimodal approach to language learning and processing, Gabriella Vigliocco](https://aovivo.abralin.org/en/lives/gabriella-vigliocco-2/)
  <details><summary>My thoughts</summary>A reminder that real language is gesture, sound and context, not just text. Great counterpoint to text-only models.</details>

## Cognition & Neuroscience

### Language and the brain

- [Brain-based language networks, Evelina Fedorenko](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=pWnR1aIfXTs)
  <details><summary>My thoughts</summary>Fascinating evidence that language has its own dedicated brain network. A must-watch for neuro-linguistics.</details>
- [Language and thought, Asifa Majid](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=fuPsNAXi1W8)
  <details><summary>My thoughts</summary>Explores how much the language you speak shapes the way you perceive the world. Cross-linguistic examples are great.</details>
- [The neurocognitive consequences of bilingualism, Mirjana Bozic](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=TgSzvvCrLno)
  <details><summary>My thoughts</summary>What speaking two languages does to the brain, with the myths separated from the evidence.</details>

### Brain, ageing & computation

- [The resilient brain: cognition and ageing, Lorraine Tyler](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=y4GaxxlJHFs)
  <details><summary>My thoughts</summary>A hopeful take on how the brain adapts as we age.</details>
- [How to study the brain from a computational view, Peter Dayan](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=CttxFk4BYrM)
  <details><summary>My thoughts</summary>A clear overview of what computational models can and cannot tell us about the brain.</details>
- [Science meets music, Peter Dayan](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=xdKAJkNZYUM)
  <details><summary>My thoughts</summary>A lighter talk on why music affects us the way it does, seen through learning and prediction.</details>

### Research methods

- [Science: how not to do it, Bob Carlyon](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=8DGqAj6tWgk)
  <details><summary>My thoughts</summary>Funny and useful. A good checklist of research pitfalls to avoid in my own work.</details>
